lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: An early sign of their secret understanding and engagement.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Elizabeth's beloved Flush welcomes her home, a private domestic image.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert's affectionate close to one of the earliest letters.

lines.text: Here is a distress for me, dearest!
lines.note: The crisis of Flush being stolen, an ordeal they share.

lines.text: Poor Flush—how sorry I am for you, my Ba!
lines.note: Robert's sympathy for Elizabeth after Flush's theft.

lines.text: Dearest, you are a prophet, I suppose—there can be no denying it.
lines.note: Elizabeth's family is suddenly ordered away, forcing their plans.

lines.text: You will only expect a few words—what will those be?
lines.note: Robert's reflection on their wedding day.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth's account of the strain and relief of the wedding day.

lines.text: I feel so as if I had slipped down over the wall into somebody’s garden—I feel ashamed.
lines.note: Elizabeth's dizzy sense of having slipped into a new life.

lines.text: You take my words from me—I ‘exult’ in the irrevocability of this precious bestowal of yourself on me—come what will my life has borne flower and fruit—it is a glorious, successful, felicitous life, I thank God and you.
First, God is to be thanked for this great joy of hearing that you are better, my ever dearest—it is a joy that floats over all the other emotions.
lines.note: Elizabeth's gratitude and anxiety about her father after the marriage.

lines.text: Is this my last letter to you, ever dearest?
lines.note: Her last letter before they leave together for Italy.
